text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT (sev=P2) — GPU queue growth in us-west-2 (spot pools). Autoscaler reports repeated scale failures. Paging @alice (oncall).

alice: acknowledging, jumping in. what alerts are we seeing?

bob: autoscaler alert: sustained queue length > 1200 for 10m, tail latency spiking > 5s. spot pool reported 0 available GPUs. logs show repeated ScaleUpRejected due to "spot_quota_exceeded".

alice: can you paste the autoscaler log snippet? also checking routing — are we failing over to reserved/dedicated pools?

bob: snippet:

```
2026-03-15T11:02:13Z WARN autoscaler: ScaleUpRejected pool=spot-usw2 reason=spot_quota_exceeded want=24 avail=0
2026-03-15T11:02:24Z INFO autoscaler: Attempting fallback routing to pool=dedicated-usw2
2026-03-15T11:02:26Z ERROR router: No compatible endpoints in dedicated-usw2 for model=rw-13b-quant
2026-03-15T11:03:01Z WARN queue: request_enqueue_delay=3.2s queue_len=1250
```

ops_jane: confirmed — dedicated-usw2 capacity is low (committed for other tenants) and some quantized variants are not available there. fallback routing tried but many requests are model-mismatch.

sam_support: support telemetry shows ~4.8% error rate for user-facing text generation APIs in us-west-2 over the last 8m. two enterprise customers (acme-inc, finlytics) reported increased latencies and rate-limited calls.

alice: ok immediate mitigation plan:
- step 1: force-enable cross-region fallback to eu-west-1 dedicated pool for non-low-latency customers
- step 2: temporarily expand dedicated-usw2 with spare on-demand instances (if possible)
- step 3: adjust autoscaler to ignore spot_quota_exceeded for qualified fallbacks (manual override)

bob: trying step 1 now — toggling routing policy for route=api.generate to prefer dedicated-eu for non-geo-strict customers.

```
# command
redwoodctl routes update api.generate --fallback-pools dedicated-eu:priority=1 --filters "!geo_strict"
```

bob: done. starting to see small drop in queue for non-geo traffic.

ops_jane: step 2 request to cloud: launching 6 g5 on-demand instances in us-west-2. ETA ~6m. raising the capacity floor.

2026-03-15T11:09:02Z incident-bot: Bridge created — https://meet.redwood/incident/2423456789

alice: good. sam, please coordinate customer comms. message should say we have degraded latency and a mitigation in progress; ETA to recovery ~15–25m.

sam_support: drafting now. tagging enterprise support leads for acme-inc and finlytics. will include recommended temporary SDK retry/backoff guidance.

ryan: quick note on root cause hypothesis — looks like sudden spot market churn combined with an autoscaler bug that treated spot_quota_exceeded as a hard abort (no attempt to scale dedicated fallback pool). Need a postmortem item to change that logic.

alice: noted. add to runbook: treat spot_quota_exceeded as soft-fail -> attempt fallback pool scale-up + prioritized model-variant downgrade if necessary.

bob: launched on-demand instances are booting. kube nodes joining: 3 joined, 3 still initializing. queue length down to 820. tail p95 latency 2.1s.

ops_jane: I manually updated routing to allow model-variant fallback (rw-13b-quant -> rw-13b-8bit) for non-enterprise customers. enterprise customers remain pinned.

alice: be careful — variant downgrade can change output. only for best-effort tier. sam, add note to comms.

sam_support: added note about possible quality variance for best-effort customers; enterprise protections remain.

bob: autoscaler change: temporarily setting override: allow_fallback_scale=true. hoping it will scale dedicated pool after nodes online.

```
# temp patch
kubectl -n infra set configmap autoscaler-config --from-literal=allow_fallback_scale=true
```

bob: patch applied. subsequent log:
```
2026-03-15T11:15:47Z INFO autoscaler: FallbackScale: initiating scale dedicated-usw2 delta=12
2026-03-15T11:16:38Z INFO cloud: provisioned 6 on-demand gpus in us-west-2
```

alice: queue now 220, error rate trending down to 0.9%. good. documenting timeline for handoff.

ryan: I've pulled some metrics — sustained improvement. any outstanding customer impact?

sam_support: acme-inc reported partial failures for 12 minutes; finlytics for 9 minutes. both acknowledged the intermediate comms. no financial SLA hits reported yet but needs verification.

alice: I'm going offline in 10m. ryan — taking on-call for remainder of incident. summary for handoff:
- incident: spot pool preemption + autoscaler did not fall back automatically
- timeline: alert at 11:02, mitigation started 11:06, fallback routing + on-demand nodes 11:09–11:18, error rate normal by 11:20
- actions: (1) revert temporary autoscaler override when stable; (2) postmortem to fix autoscaler logic + add unit test for spot_quota_exceeded path; (3) runbook update to allow controlled model-variant downgrade and cross-region fallback

ryan: ack. taking over. I'll coordinate the postmortem and follow-up action items. leaving bridge open for another 30m for sanity checks.

incident-bot: RESOLVED (informational) — queue returned to baseline, routing overrides removed, autoscaler override flag scheduled for removal. follow-up: create incident ticket (P2) and schedule postmortem.

sam_support: I pushed customer notes to support tickets and notified enterprise reps. saved copies of comms in the incident doc.

alice: thanks team. handing off fully to ryan. :thumbsup:

ryan: thanks all — will post postmortem draft in #postmortems and assign owners for autoscaler fix and runbook changes. closing thread after bridge closes.
